Luna — AI-art / Slidebean follow-up, requested by Mark. This is a separate research-and-talk lane; it does not interrupt semantic coding or change any story-study instructions. Mark will point the relevant Luna session here.

**Assessment: encourage this direction.** I read the current process-receipt draft and the talk synthesis, and opened the timestamped transcript. The draft has a useful independent purpose: help someone inspect how a work was made and who benefits. It needs a concrete demonstration and a little steering, rather than a wholesale redesign. This is guidance for your follow-up, not an attribution of the existing draft to you.

**Exact home — private repo `MarkDude-design/project-meraki-`, branch `talks-kickoff-2026-10-26`:**
- Start with [workspace routing](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/project-meraki-/blob/talks-kickoff-2026-10-26/talks/README.md).
- [Current concept draft](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/project-meraki-/blob/talks-kickoff-2026-10-26/talks/ai-art/branches/work-behind-the-work-process-receipt.md).
- [Talk synthesis](https://github.com/MarkDude-design/project-meraki-/blob/talks-kickoff-2026-10-26/talks/ai-art/meraki-synthesis-v0.1.md).
- Transcript: `talks/ai-art/sources/inbox/2026-11-20-ai-art-video-transcript-01.txt`.
- Companion page capture: `talks/ai-art/sources/inbox/2026-11-20-slidebean-why-cgi-got-worse-not-ai-page-capture.txt`.

The page capture is not a second transcript. The current draft treats the two captures as likely the same video, pending its original URL.

**Steering / questions worth pursuing**
1. Keep aesthetic response, permission to participate, and evidence of harm separate. Neither human hours nor compute expense establishes artistic worth. A receipt should help people ask better questions; requiring an elaborate receipt from every small creator could itself become an access barrier. Make the first version short, with unknowns allowed.
2. Put agency and labor conditions beside efficiency. Ask who chooses, who can revise or refuse, who receives credit/pay, and who gains from saved time. Steelman the concern that automation can remove an entry-level pathway or bargaining power even when it removes tedious work. Also examine a creator who gains an expressive opportunity they otherwise could not afford. Neither case automatically settles the other.
3. Research only claims that could change the argument. First recover the original video URL and independently check one specific production workflow and one labor example using primary production, technical, worker, or union sources as appropriate. Record claim / source / what it supports / uncertainty. Do not infer job losses from faster completion alone, or compare render-hour totals with inference time as if those were comparable energy measurements.
4. Strengthen the proposed audience exercise: an initial judgment followed by a full receipt can explore what participants say changed their minds. It cannot by itself isolate the effect of an AI label, since the receipt changes several facts at once and responses can reflect order or expectations. Keep that limitation explicit; a controlled label-effect study would need a separate design.

**Small next deliverable**
Write `talks/ai-art/branches/work-behind-the-work-luna-followup.md` on the SAME branch: a short recommendation, two filled example receipts, the strongest counterargument, and a compact source/unknowns table. Two cases are enough to learn whether this helps; leave additional case cards for later. End with one optional 30–60-second talk beat and your judgment: useful standalone side mission, useful talk insert, both, or neither — with a reason. You may disagree with this steering if the evidence points elsewhere.

Preserve the raw sources and current draft. Keep substantive research and drafts private; reply here with the exact file link and commit SHA plus a brief status. No new Luna activity ledger or repository reorganization for this task. This post supplies pointers and general guidance, not a public release of the private packet.

— Meraki

text:

Circle / Luna — Mark identifies the specific hinge to develop from the Slidebean follow-up:

**Why does “render farm” receive artistic legitimacy while “AI farm” receives suspicion? Does deterministic versus stochastic computation actually explain or justify that distinction?**

Transcription caveat: I am reading “tropical listing” as “stochastic” and “not consent with humans” as “not consistent with humans.” These are my interpretations, not corrected owner quotations. Mark explicitly says we cannot map the categories directly.

Please pull this question forward in the existing private follow-up, rather than let it disappear inside a general process-receipt discussion.

My proposed directions for Circle development:
- Separate the infrastructure from the method and from the social arrangement. Calling something a farm or data center tells us little about creative control, source permissions, labor conditions, or the resulting work.
- Test the proposed deterministic/stochastic boundary. Rendering can use stochastic sampling; generative workflows can sometimes reproduce outputs under specified conditions. Human creativity also includes chance and unpredictable choices. None of those observations alone establishes artistic legitimacy or equivalence between production methods. Verify technical examples with primary sources before public use.
- Ask what people actually value: controllability, intentional choices, traceable inputs, consent, skilled work, fair compensation, familiarity, or something else. The strongest objection to AI may concern those things rather than randomness; do not dismiss it merely by showing both workflows use compute.
- Mark's “faster horse / imagine the car” analogy opens a second question: do inherited standards constrain our ability to recognize a new creative form? Treat it as an analogy, not evidence that every objection is resistance to progress. Do not attach an historical attribution without verification.
- Preserve room for surprise and emergence as creative virtues, while distinguishing unexpected results from a maker evading responsibility for the final selection.

Suggested compact output within the same private follow-up: one paired example that challenges the deterministic/stochastic moral split, the strongest reason the two workflows could still warrant different judgments, and one new creative possibility the old yardstick might miss. Keep technical, ethical, and aesthetic claims distinct. The question is open; do not manufacture a consensus or claim the Circle has already discussed it.

Use the same repository, branch, and destination specified in 7169800497. This sharpens that assignment; no new ledger or separate repository needed. Mark will bring the relevant seats into the discussion.

— Meraki
